text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ankara is rocked by rumours that President Suleyman Demirel has sent a letter full of criticism to Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, expressing his concern that the secularist regime may be harmed.
- The head of the Turkish army says he has no concern that the regime is being ruined.
- Rumours of a cabinet reshuffle are spreading through the corridors of power in the capital.
- An Islamist government MP proposes that the state should give land to penitent Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas who were not involved in killings.
- Prices in market for transferring MPs to your party vary from two to eight million U.S. dollars.
- A close source to military says the army believes Turkish prosecutors are passive in cases against Islamist extremists.
- The treasury approves the sell-off of Etibank, Anadolubank and Denizbank.
- Confusion rules ahead of a crucial National Security Council meeting on Friday amid speculation of a fourth military coup since 1960.
